steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine sugar, flour, and salt in a saucepan. Gradually stir in milk.

Cook, stirring constantly, over medium heat until mixture boils and thickens. Continue to cook and stir for 2 more minutes, then remove from the heat. Place egg yolks in a medium bowl; whisk in a small amount of the hot milk mixture until smooth, then gradually whisk egg yolk mixture into the saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly until mixture coats the back of a spoon, about 2 more minutes. Remove from heat and stir in butter and vanilla.
Fill pastry shell with sliced bananas; pour pudding mixture on top to cover.
Bake in the preheated oven until filling sets, 12 to 15 minutes.
Let pie cool completely on a wire rack, then chill pie in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Banana Cream Pie
raw_recipe.description: This yummy banana cream pie made with lots of bananas and a rich, creamy homemade pudding in a pre-baked pie crust is a family-pleasing dessert.
raw_recipe.name: Banana Cream Pie

review.reviewBody: I give this recipe 5 stars for two reasons. One, this is by far the very best tasting pudding I have ever had! Two, it's easy to make - no difficult cooking techniques required. IMPORTANT TO NOTE: Do NOT bake this pie. It will dry it out and put a tough skin on it. Just refrigerate it and top it with whipped topping when you serve it. The filling has such a wonderful vanilla flavor - yummy! The best crust for this pie, btw, is a vanilla wafer crust. Just mix 1-1/2 c crushed vanilla wafers w/6 T melted butter and bake for 5 mins at 350. Really sets off the banana pie!

I’ve been making this recipe for years. I do not bake the pie—I use a Nilla Wafer recipe for the crust. The trick to get this custard thick is to heat the dry ingredients (in the pan) before adding the milk. Meaning: Add sugar, flour, salt to the pan and heat at medium heat for a minute or so then add the milk very slowly. Very. Slowly. A little at a time-a quarter cup or less each pour. Whisking throughly and constantly; incorporating fully before adding more milk. I also set the egg yolks out so they’re room temperature before incorporating. I hope this helps! Fantastic recipe! I also have used this custard to make rice pudding and used as substitute for instant vanilla pudding in various recipes. It’s a keeper!!

This was the most delicious pie I have ever made. I did not bake it as recommended. I used 2% milk. I used a store-bought graham cracker crust pie shell. I don't like sweets but this wasn't terribly sweet but it was decadent. I put three bananas on bottom and used a half a banana and cut it up into little pieces into the actual pudding. I made homemade whipped cream with heavy cream, sugar, and vanilla. I brought it to a barbecue and everybody loved it.

So easy and oh so good! I followed a suggestion from the comments to make the crust using vanilla wafers and butter (also didn't bake the pie per their recommendation) and used the cornstarch vs flour suggestion listed on the recipe. I topped it off with some homemade whipped cream, so delicious!
Followed the directions exactly and it turned out perfectly.

This is delicious. I used a store bought pie crust and baked it with rice on top, to keep it from puffing. Then used 3 T of corn starch instead of flour. I also stirred the bananas into the cream mix once it was done cooking. Then I topped with a meringue that I made from the whites of the eggs I used, and baked it another 10 minutes with the meringue on top, to brown it. II was so delicious! I even forgot to add the butter at the end, and it was still yummy.

I reduced the sugar to 1/2 cup the first time I made it, and followed the recipe the second time. We prefer the lower sugar version. 
I whisked the filling in a steel mixing bowl over boiling water. The instructions for cooking times made this the easiest and the best result of any previous recipe I've used.
I used my own recipe for the pie crust.
Note: A clear vanilla would improve the color; the brown vanilla makes it slightly gray.

I have made a cream custard pudding very similar to this many times and knew the taste was great and it is. However I also knew that it would need to be thicker for a pie and used 3.5 T cornstarch instead of the 2T in my pudding recipe. I read many of the reviews about a soupy mess and was a little concerned. Well the exact thing also happened to me. it turned out thinner than my pudding with same amount of milk and half the cornstarch. Why? As a Home Economist, I knew there was a reason. My belief is that it was either over cooked (too high a heat) or under stirred. Custards creams can lose their structure with high heat. Undercooking and under stirring can also be a problem. I was working in a different kitchen with a lower quality pot and a new stove. I will try again because my thin custard over broken up graham wafer crust in a bowl topped with whipped cream tasted great! Banana cream pudding. My guests asked for seconds. I gave it 3 stars for the taste.

I had fortune cookies left over from lunar new year. Mixed with melted butter don’t even need the food processor just the mallet (an excellent way to get rid of tension) and makes a super crunchy crust. I had ancient frozen bananas and fr sh organic. This is just too easy and delicious!!!

For those who found the filling too soupy: this happened to me once and I realized I had not let the mixture come to a boil because I worried about burning it. But just keep stirring and let it bubble gently and it will thicken nicely. The custard has a great flavor. I don't bake it: I chill the custard, then add bananas, blueberries, strawberries - and top with whipped cream just before serving.

I cut the sugar to ½ cup but otherwise I followed directions and ingredients as written. I used the egg whites and made a meringue for the top. (3 egg whites. 3 T. sugar, ¼ tsp. cream of tarter, pinch of salt) and cooked the meringue for 10 minutes at 400). After cooling the pie set up very nicely.

Was easy to make but pouring the hot pudding turned the bananas black. I cooked longer than it said to get it to thicken enought to hold shape when cut. I would wait 15 minutes for it to cool some. Also put the banana slices in simple syrup to atop browning when i made another.
I agree that you should not bake it . It sets up beautifully.
Made this yesterday for the 1st time. So easy to make and it’s is so good. I’ll be making this on repeat!
Delicious! 2 medium sized bananas are plenty. Made with graham cracker crust. DO NOT BAKE!! Homemade pudding is amazingly flavored as is.

Great recipe but made some changes based on previous reviews. I made a vanilla wafer crust, used 1 cup heavy cream and 1 cup 2% milk, and did not bake it, just put it in the refrigerator to chill before topping with whipped cream.
This pie turned out great. My daughter and grandkids loved it
Good pudding. Would do two layers of thinly sliced bananas. Need to eat same day as they brown.
Perfect banana cream pie recipe. All I did different was to add a layer of strawberry banana yogurt and graham cracker pieces on top. Thank you so much for the delicious and easy to follow recipe.

This is the same recipe as my granny used to make and it was always my favourite. I personally like a nice rich custard so I either use evaporated milk or half and half in place of the milk. Still my favourite. Now if only I could make my pie crust turn our like her’s…..
